bullets: Ignoring the 'tat' in systems thinking forces a rebuild from scratch a year later — the failure mode of skipping foundational details.
Two years of systems thinking work sharpens focus on leverage points — the highest-impact places to intervene in a system.
Reliability and sustainability are intertwined, not separate concerns — the second-order effects of decisions are where most people miss the real impact.
Sustainability and systems thinking intersect through second-order effects — the part most people overlook when evaluating tradeoffs.
Reliability crosscuts everything in systems design — tradeoffs around it are not isolated but pervasive across all system aspects.
A practical starting point is to pick one of the EDSV cover rates and run it for two weeks — a concrete experiment to internalize systems thinking principles.
Once you internalize the top-level framing, the rest of the decisions get easier — a cascading simplification effect from core principles.
